skill.name: api-organization
skill.description: Organizes TypeScript API layers with endpoint types, centralized URL builders, authenticated clients, admin checks, and protected endpoint wrappers for a Next.js Supabase app.
skill.summary: Guide for building type-safe API endpoints, clients, auth flows, and protected wrappers in a Next.js Supabase app.
skill.author: BOM-98

security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives from Markdown documentation examples, including TypeScript template literals, placeholder URLs, and environment variable names. I found no executable scripts, command execution behavior, prompt injection text, or evidence of credential exfiltration intent.

content.value_statement: API code often becomes inconsistent across clients, URLs, and types. This skill provides a repeatable TypeScript structure for endpoints, clients, auth, and role checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains the five-file API layout under src/lib/api.
Shows how to define endpoint parameter, response, and body types.
Defines centralized endpoint URL grouping and naming conventions.
Demonstrates Supabase auth headers and middleware integration.
Describes admin role validation and family-scoped access patterns.
Guides migration from direct fetch calls to protected endpoint wrappers.
limitations: Tailored to a Next.js and Supabase TypeScript architecture.
Does not create real credentials, projects, or database tables.
Examples use placeholders and require project-specific adaptation.
Does not replace a backend authorization security review.

use_cases.title: Add a New API Domain
use_cases.description: Plan endpoint types, URL builders, and protected wrappers for a new feature area.

use_cases.title: Standardize Existing API Calls
use_cases.description: Convert scattered direct requests into shared typed clients and centralized endpoint definitions.

use_cases.title: Review Authenticated Access Patterns
use_cases.description: Check that regular and admin endpoints follow Supabase session and role validation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Endpoint Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one new API resource.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define endpoint types for a new resources API with list, get, create, update, and delete operations.

prompt_templates.title: Build Endpoint URL Definitions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for centralized URL builders.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design API_ENDPOINTS entries for a nested category products API with clear naming and parameter rules.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Direct API Calls
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refactor from scattered fetch calls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a migration from direct fetch calls to typed protected endpoint wrappers and shared API client helpers.

prompt_templates.title: Design Admin Protected Access
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request involving role checks and Supabase auth.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design admin-only API access with Supabase session headers, role validation, error handling, and typed wrappers.

output_examples.input: Add a new resources API domain to the project.
output: A plan for response, request body, and parameter types.
A centralized URL grouping for list, get, create, update, and delete operations.
Wrapper guidance that uses the existing authenticated client helpers.

output_examples.input: Refactor existing direct requests into the shared API pattern.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist that moves request URLs into endpoint definitions and routes access through protected wrappers.
An access plan that validates admin roles before sensitive operations and keeps tenant data scoped by database policies.

best_practices: Define endpoint types before implementing URL builders or wrappers.
Keep all endpoint URLs centralized and grouped by domain.
Validate admin access before any privileged API operation.
anti_patterns: Do not scatter direct fetch calls across components and actions.
Do not hardcode API base URLs outside the endpoint configuration.
Do not bypass shared auth helpers for protected endpoints.

faq.question: What framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets TypeScript applications using Next.js, Supabase Auth, and a shared API client layer.

faq.question: Can it create a full API implementation?
faq.answer: It provides structure and examples, but the project still needs real routes, data models, and tests.

faq.question: Does it support admin-only endpoints?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes separate admin client behavior with role checks before privileged requests.

faq.question: Does it require Supabase?
faq.answer: The documented auth flow is Supabase-specific, although the organization pattern can inform other auth systems.

faq.question: Where should API code live?
faq.answer: The skill expects API support code to live under src/lib/api with five coordinated files.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
